To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concentration of serum albumin increases rapidly after birth in the piglet, and that synthesis of albumin in liver slices is 5- to10-fold greater at 4-10 days of age than at birth.
the rate of albumin synthesis in the liver of newborn pigs is low but increases rapidly after birth to reach adult levels in about 1 week.

the rate of albumin synthesis by the pig liver increases abruptly at or near birth and that this increase in the rate is sufficient to account fully for the rising serum albumin concentration of the postnatal animal.

the development and application of a method to measure the synthesis of albumins in the liver of newborn pigs.
the synthesis of serum albumin (SA) by the liver in the perinatal piglet.
the synthesis and secretion of albumin in vivo and in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the piglet, the rate of synthesis and concentration of serum albumin increases abruptly at birth and that this increase is due to a selective alteration of the pattern of protein synthesis in liver.
, as the piglet matures, the rate of synthesis and secretion of albumin increases sharply, and this is sufficient to account quantitatively for the rising level of serum albumin in the postnatal pig.
the increase in serum albumin concentration in the newborn piglet results from an increase in the rate, and perhaps the extent, of synthesis of albumins by the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of albumin synthesis increases abruptly at the time of birth, in proportion to the increase in serum albumin.
the rate of albumin synthesis increases abruptly in the perinatal period, and that the increase is selective and sufficient to account for rising serum albumin levels in the postnatal period.
the synthesis of serum albumin is selectively enhanced in the postnatal pig.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated a significant increase in albumin synthesis in the liver of postnatal pigs.
the liver is the major site for albumin synthesis, which is increased in the postnatal period.
